analysis: Valproic acid is primarily known as an anticonvulsant and mood-stabilizing drug. It is recognized for several side effects and risks. Firstly, it is not an enzyme inducer; rather, it is an enzyme inhibitor, which means it can increase the levels of other drugs metabolized by the liver. This makes option (opa) the correct choice as it is false. Secondly, valproic acid is associated with weight gain, which can lead to obesity, confirming option (opb) as true. Thirdly, it can cause hirsutism due to its effects on hormone levels, making option (opc) true as well. Lastly, valproic acid is a known teratogen and is linked to neural tube defects, thus option (opd) is also true. Therefore, the only statement that is incorrect is that valproic acid is an enzyme inducer.
